$comment: Impossible-transition policy (D3-02). Config, not code: this file is read from disk at runtime,
so the speed tolerance, the confidence thresholds and the alert severity all move without a
rebuild. anomaly.test.ts (AC 3) proves it by scoring one identical segment under two policies.
THE RULE THAT SHAPES THIS WHOLE FILE, and the one thing most likely to be got backwards:
every quantity this policy is compared against is a LOWER bound. `roadDistanceKm` is OSRM's
FASTEST path, so it is the least distance the vehicle can have driven; therefore
`roadDistanceKm / elapsed` is the least speed it can have averaged, and `expectedTravelTimeS`
is the least time the trip can have taken. A transition is called impossible only when even
that most generous reading is unreachable. The converse is NOT a clean bill of health: a
transition that looks fine against the fastest path may still be impossible on the road the
vehicle actually took. D2-08's `TraceSegment.impliedSpeedKmh` documents the same quantity as
an UPPER bound and must not be used here — see the note on issue #25.
A finding under this policy is never an accusation. There is no live VAHAN or SARTHI link, so
nothing here can confirm that a registration exists or who holds it. The output says two
sightings are inconsistent with a single vehicle, and names the innocent explanation beside the
guilty one every time.
Two independent feasibility tests, both on the lower-bound side. A segment must fail only ONE
to be impossible; they catch different things.
maxPlausibleKmh 140 is the fastest sustained average this detector will concede on Indian
roads. NHAI's highest notified expressway limit for cars is 120 km/h and the ordinary
national-highway limit is 100; 140 is deliberately above both, because the cost of a false
'impossible' here is an officer told two vehicles share a registration when one of them was
simply speeding. It is a physical ceiling, not an enforcement threshold, and this detector is
not a speed-enforcement tool.
graphSpeedTolerance 1.35 asks the second question: did the vehicle beat OSRM's free-flow
estimate for the fastest path by more than 35 percent? Free-flow already assumes no traffic,
no signals and no stops, so beating it at all is unusual; beating it by a third is not
driving. It catches the short, dense hop that maxPlausibleKmh cannot — 2 km in 20 s is only
360 km/h over a distance where the road graph says 180 s, and both tests fire, but 2 km in
70 s is 103 km/h through city streets the graph prices at 180 s, which only this test sees.
minElapsedSeconds 5 is a guard, not a tolerance. Below it the elapsed time is dominated by
PTS quantisation and frame cadence rather than by travel, and a divide-by-almost-zero would
manufacture an impossible speed out of arithmetic. Such a segment is reported as
`indeterminate`, never as feasible and never as impossible.
Which explanation is more likely, once the transition is impossible. The thresholds are the
estate's measured OCR range, not round numbers: D2-01 read 0 plates exactly across a
120-instance hand-labelled sample, and the five legible strings the live run produced scored
0.449, 0.503, 0.732, 0.627 and 0.56. A 'high confidence' bar of 0.9 would never be met by
anything this estate produces and the clone branch would be dead code; a bar of 0.5 would
call the whole estate high-confidence. 0.75 and 0.60 straddle the measured range.
maxNeighbourDistance 2 is D2-04's measured operating point and the ceiling this project does
not cross: docs/fuzzy-matching.md section 6 measures d<=2 at 99.9 percent recall and 100
percent precision, d<=3 at 91.2 percent precision, and d<=4 collapsing to 54.8 percent with
unrelated plates matching. Two vehicles accused of sharing a registration because a matcher
was generous is the failure this project cannot afford.
truncationDominanceRatio 0.5: when at least half a candidate's weighted distance came from
`tailChars` rather than substitution, the shorter read is a clean prefix of the longer one —
the same vehicle read badly, which D2-04 measured as this estate's dominant failure and
prices at 0.35 per character. That is a misread every time and never a clone.
repeatPairsForClone 2: one impossible transition is an anomaly, two on the same pair of
cameras with the same reads is a pattern. Cloning is a standing arrangement — the same
registration on two vehicles both in daily use — so it recurs, while a single OCR accident
does not. Below the threshold the verdict is `undetermined`, which is an honest third state
and not a euphemism for clean.
Cloning suspicion is escalated as its own alert type, separate from the watchlist queue in
`alerts`: a watchlist hit says 'this vehicle is wanted', and this says 'these two sightings
cannot both be one vehicle'. Different claim, different evidence, different action.
severity 'medium' by default, and configurable. Deliberately not 'high': the identification
on this estate is fuzzy far more often than not, and D2-06's rule applies unchanged — a
severity is never raised by a model's opinion. `minLinkConfidence` is the second guard.
D2-08 measured mean link confidence for recoverable reads at 0.34 to 0.59, so an alert built
on two links at 0.34 is two possibilities rather than two identifications. 0.5 keeps the
alert for the upper half of that measured range and reports the rest as a finding without
escalating it.
cropUrlExpiresInS 900 matches config/alert-policy.json. The URL is minted at read time and
never stored: a stored signed URL is a credential with an expiry rotting in the database.
